newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Group formed to bid for NZ Mangahao hydro station.
newsitem.headline: Group formed to bid for NZ Mangahao hydro station.

text.p: Horowhenua power company Electra said on Wednesday it was part of a group formed to bid for the Mangahao hydro power station, near Levin in New Zealand's lower North Island.

The announcement of the bidding group follows the National-New Zealand First coalition government's confirmation on Monday that it plans to sell eight small Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ) power stations.

TransAlta New Zealand (63 percent owned by Canada's TransAlta Corp and unlisted Manawatu power company CentralPower are also in the bidding group, along with lower North Island Maori interests Mua-Upoko, Ngati Raukawa, Ngati Toa Rangatira, Rangitane Ki Manawatu and Te Ati Awa Ki Waikanae.
The Mangahao hydro dam and power station produces approximately 26 megawatts of electricity.

Spokesperson for the bidding group Robert Steele said an interest in the dam meant greater protection for members of the group against energy market uncertainty, and control of a local energy asset by locally-based companies.
